title: Ghosts in the Hull
logline: A scrap yard mechanic discovers the shiny new freighters being sold to local merchants are actually just painted-over warships from an old, devastating conflict.

roles.description: Always sees patterns, and this time they are right.
Sells 'refurbished' ships at a premium, hiding their dark past.
A sprawling orbital lot full of seemingly pristine vessels.
A 'new' freighter that still has hidden torpedo tubes.

public_situation: The {role:slick_salesman} is making a fortune selling incredibly durable, cheap freighters to local merchants.
private_truth: The freighters are decommissioned military vessels that were supposed to be scrapped, and their combat automations are waking up.

beats.public_change: The mechanic is fired for asking too many questions about the ship schematics.

missions.reason: The mechanic hires the pilot to do a deep structural scan of one of the freighters to find the hidden weapon hardpoints.
missions.private_fact: The scan will trigger the ship's dormant defense protocols.

beats.public_change: The salesman puts out a hit on the mechanic, claiming they stole industrial secrets.

missions.reason: The mechanic needs the pilot to deliver a massive data-dump of the ship's real history to the shipyard's public feed.
missions.private_fact: The history shows these ships were used in civilian massacres.

beats.public_change: The public is outraged, but the salesman tries to silence the mechanic permanently.

missions.reason: The mechanic asks the pilot to extract the master logic core from the shipyard to prove the ships are still dangerous.
missions.private_fact: The salesman has rigged the core to self-destruct.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot has the logic core. They can expose the salesman's deadly fraud, or sell the core back to them to keep the secret.

options.label: Give the core to the mechanic
Sell the core to the salesman

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot helps expose the salesman.
resolutions.summary: The ships are grounded and recalled. The salesman is arrested for trafficking military hardware, and the mechanic is vindicated.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved the cheap new freighters in the sector were actually repainted death machines.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot sells the core to the salesman.
resolutions.summary: The salesman buries the evidence. The ships continue to be sold, until one eventually wakes up and destroys a civilian dock.
The mechanic is quietly murdered by shipyard security. The blood-soaked ships are sold as family haulers.

loose_threads.detail: The serial numbers on the warship hulls match a fleet that supposedly jumped into a black hole twenty years ago.
The salesman mentions they bought the scrap hulls from an anonymous 'admiral' who demanded payment in raw thorium.

radio_hooks: Amazing deals on 'lightly used' freighters at the local shipyard!
Local merchants report strange software glitches in newly purchased ships.

voice_direction.paranoid_mechanic: Hushed, very fast cadence, constantly shifting tone.
